advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid re-running the network divergence probe once per event in multi-event transactions (probe once per transaction/commit instead).
evidence: _seam.py:488: `_refuse_unpublishable_store(tracker)` is called inside `finalize_event`.
txn.py:533 and txn.py:553 both call `finalize_event(...)` within one transaction (STATUS then EDIT), each triggering a fresh `write_blocking_divergence` and thus a fresh `git fetch`.
completion_txn.py:60 and delete.py:132/240 also route through the same seam.
advisory.finding: The divergence probe runs its full sequence (including a network fetch) once per EVENT, so a multi-event transaction (STATUS + EDIT) fetches the remote multiple times in a single logical write.
scenarios: A transition-with-assignee transaction performs the remote fetch and merge-base probe twice for what is one atomic commit.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the finalize_event docstring (src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:474-477) so its CommandError enumeration also covers the no-common-ancestor unpublishable-store refusal added at line 488.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:474-477 docstring: 'raises :class:`CommandError` ONLY when ``identity.require_authenticated`` is on and a NON-exempt event cannot be signed (the write-gate)'

src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:488 adds `_refuse_unpublishable_store(tracker)` and src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:501 raises CommandError for the unpublishable-store refusal, a second raise path not covered by the docstring's 'ONLY'
docs/documentation-policy.md:16 Comments role: correction method is 'Update or remove the comment with the code'; exclusions include code restatements that go stale
advisory.finding: The finalize_event docstring states CommandError is raised ONLY for the write-gate (unsigned non-exempt event), but the change adds _refuse_unpublishable_store(tracker) which raises CommandError for a no-common-ancestor DIVERGED store. The docstring's enumerated raise contract is now inaccurate.
scenarios: A contributor reading finalize_event relies on the docstring's 'ONLY' clause to reason about which callers must handle CommandError and misses the new pre-commit refusal path.
advisory.suggested_fix: Amend the docstring to note that finalize_event also raises CommandError before committing when the tracker has no common ancestor with the fetched shared branch (via _refuse_unpublishable_store), so the 'ONLY' write-gate clause is no longer the sole raise condition.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a write via finalize_event in an ordinary PUSH_PENDING (local-ahead, common-ancestor) state is NOT refused: the write commits (HEAD advances) and raises no RebarError.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:265: `if not no_common_ancestor:` / `return None` — the sole guard keeping common-ancestor divergence writable
docs/concurrency.md: 'The narrow no-common-ancestor refusal is different ... ordinary local-ahead push-pending remains best-effort'

The pre-existing pin `tests/unit/test_gate_store_freshness.py::test_a_stale_store_does_not_make_an_ordinary_write_raise` asserts on `push.push_tickets_branch`, not on the new `_refuse_unpublishable_store`/`finalize_event` seam (tests/unit/test_gate_store_freshness.py:257), so it does not cover this diff's new gate.

ABSENCE: no added test drives a write via `rebar.comment`/`create_ticket` while local-ahead with a COMMON ancestor and asserts it succeeds (HEAD advances, no RebarError). Named violating input: a tracker one commit ahead of origin/tickets sharing a common ancestor (the exact state `test_fsck_reports_push_pending_and_stays_exit_0` builds, but which only runs `fsck`, never a write).
advisory.finding: No regression test proves the narrow refusal does NOT over-refuse an ordinary PUSH_PENDING / common-ancestor write routed through finalize_event. The design's load-bearing property is narrowness (only no-common-ancestor is refused; local-ahead and common-ancestor divergence must still write), yet only the refusal path is tested. A regression weakening `if not no_common_ancestor: return None` (line 265-266) would silently convert the store into a write outage.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_fsck_push_pending.py, add a test using repo_with_origin that makes a local-ahead-but-common-ancestor state (as test_fsck_reports_push_pending_and_stays_exit_0 does) then calls rebar.comment(seed, ...) and asserts HEAD advanced and no RebarError was raised.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests for write_blocking_divergence's differing-remote-URL allow-branch and its missing-remote-.store-compat.json allow-branch.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:227-232: `if (code_remote.returncode == 0 and tracker_remote.returncode == 0 and code_remote.stdout.strip() != tracker_remote.stdout.strip()): return None`
src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:244-255: `cat-file -e {remote_ref}:.store-compat.json ... return None` when the compat record is absent on the remote ref

ABSENCE: the only added write-side test (test_first_write_refuses_unrelated_diverged_store) exercises the same-remote, compat-present, no-common-ancestor path; neither the differing-remote branch nor the missing-remote-compat branch is exercised. Named violating input for (b): a no-common-ancestor remote ref whose tree has NO `.store-compat.json` — must NOT block — is untested.
advisory.finding: The two new allow-branches in write_blocking_divergence are untested: (a) code repo remote URL differs from tracker remote URL → return None (do not block), and (b) the fetched remote ref lacks a committed `.store-compat.json` → return None. Both are newly-added decision points that determine whether writes are ever blocked, and a regression in either could either block writes that should proceed or fail to block a genuine split-brain.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid a synchronous network `git fetch` on every ticket write in `write_blocking_divergence`; gate/cache it so ordinary writes don't pay a per-write round-trip.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:488: `_refuse_unpublishable_store(tracker)` inserted into finalize_event, the seam every writer routes through
src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:234: `fetched = run_git(tracker, "fetch", remote, refspec, check=False, timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT)`
src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:66: `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 60`

freshness.py:24 docstring: 'Staleness is defined LOCALLY — no network. A gate must not acquire a dependency on the remote being reachable' — the new write-side probe adds exactly that network dependency to every write
No memoization/cache: write_blocking_divergence re-runs the full fetch+probe on each call (freshness.py:192-262)
advisory.finding: `_refuse_unpublishable_store` (called from `finalize_event`, the single seam EVERY ticket write routes through) triggers a synchronous network `git fetch` with a 60s timeout on every write, coupling write latency/availability to remote reachability.
scenarios: A busy repo issuing many rebar writes (create/edit/transition/claim) — each write now blocks on a network fetch; under a slow or contended remote each can stall up to 60s
Remote unreachable/slow: write latency degrades across the board even though the docstring's rejected 'blanket write-refusal' path was explicitly avoided to prevent turning degradation into an outage

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Probe divergence once per logical write/batch rather than per event in `finalize_event`, so multi-event transactions and reconciler batches don't issue N network fetches.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:533 and txn.py:553: a single claim transaction calls `finalize_event(...)` twice (STATUS then EDIT) — each now triggers a fetch
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py:253: `_seam.finalize_event(...)` is called per inbound event inside the reconciler's batch translate loop
src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:234: each finalize_event -> write_blocking_divergence -> `run_git(tracker, "fetch", ...)` with no dedupe across the batch
advisory.finding: Because `finalize_event` runs `write_blocking_divergence` (with its network fetch) once PER EVENT, multi-event transactions and the reconciler's batch loop incur N network fetches for N events instead of one probe per logical operation/batch.
scenarios: Reconciler translating a batch of inbound Jira events: one network fetch per event, so wall-clock scales linearly with batch size and remote latency
Any multi-event operation (claim = STATUS+EDIT) pays two fetches for one user action

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the new network `git fetch` in `write_blocking_divergence` with the freshness module's 'no network on write/read path' invariant, or justify/bound the per-write remote fetch.
evidence: freshness.py:24-25: '**Staleness is defined LOCALLY — no network.** A gate must not acquire a dependency on the remote being reachable, and every signal needed is already on disk'
freshness.py:234: `fetched = run_git(tracker, "fetch", remote, refspec, check=False, timeout=_GIT_TIMEOUT)`

The sibling probe `_ref_divergence` deliberately does NOT fetch (freshness.py:93-94: 'Purely local: no `fetch`, so this reports what the clone's git dir ALREADY knows and never makes a gate depend on network reachability').
This runs via `_refuse_unpublishable_store` inside `finalize_event`, the shared pre-commit seam every write routes through (_seam.py:488).
blocking.finding: `write_blocking_divergence` performs a network `git fetch` on the ticket write path, breaking the module's explicit 'no network on the freshness path' invariant and adding remote-reachability latency to every write.
scenarios: Every `create`/`edit`/`transition`/`claim`/`comment` write now blocks on a remote fetch (up to `_GIT_TIMEOUT`=60s) before committing.
Slow or high-latency remotes add fetch latency to interactive ticket commands that previously touched only local disk.
